text:
ella: noticed odd rows in a customer's dashboard that look like another org's data. popped up after today's small renderer rollout.
sam: can you paste the panel link and quick repro?
ella: panel: /console/dashboards/insight/42?range=1h — switch orgs quickly and you'll see 'Login events' from org 310 in org 12's view. only visible in the streaming preview window for a few secs.
noah: staging CR went out at 07:44 (renderer v3.2.1). we also toggled prefetch envelope caching to reduce cold starts.
cheng: hmm could be envelope-level metadata being reused. our prefetch cache stores response + envelope.headers which we assumed idempotent. maybe we attached org_id as header in the envelope and didn't namespace the cache key.
ella: repro steps: 1) open org 12, 2) trigger insights, 3) click org switch to 310, 4) click back to 12 within ~200ms. ghosted rows show for ~20-40s.
sam: does the browser show mixed headers in the preview request? can you capture a HAR?
ella: HAR shows preview call returned with header "X-Envelope-Org: 310" even though request had "X-Console-Org: 12". the preview UI then renders that envelope as-is.
noah: that strongly suggests a cache key issue. PR notes mentioned we removed "org_id" from the key to increase cache hit rate. that was intended for public static snippets, but apparently it hit dynamic panels too.
cheng: spec: prefetch key components should always include (service, panel_id, org_id, auth_fingerprint). we accidentally made org_id optional for panels flagged as "staticish". this panel was misflagged.
ella: any immediate mitigation we can push? this is leaking data across tenants.
sam: quick fix: mark the insights panel as strict-cache and invalidate the prefetch cache entries for last 2 hours. also re-enable org_id in key construction for all non-whitelisted panels.
noah: i'll open a tiny hotfix to the prefetch service to attach a "cache-namespace" tag that includes org_id at write-time. also add an assert that prevents writing envelope.headers.org.* into a shared cache without org namespacing.
cheng: prefer feature-flagged rollout: enable strict namespacing in staging and 10% of prod. avoid broad cache cold starts.
devops-bot: cache-invalidate job queued for panel 42 across regions at 2026-03-19T08:30:00Z.
ella: telemetry: i saw an uptick in quota-burn for org 12 right after the flash, suspicious. could leaked rows be causing double-counting of tokens/quota?
sam: yes, if UI requests are attributed to the org that requested the view but the envelope contains another org's rows, billing telemetry might misattribute. add metric: leaked_row_count and leaked_row_source_org.
noah: logging: we should emit an event when envelope.headers.org != request.org with fields: request_org, envelope_org, panel, session_id, cache_key. flag these as P0 when envelope_org != request_org.
cheng: UX rollout note: the quick org switch button triggers multiple parallel previews; the renderer dedup logic merges responses and may swallow header corrections. need to ensure headers are canonicalized at merge boundary, not only on first write.
ella: agreed. i'll draft a short incident note for ops and customer-success in case any customers notice.
sam: long term: audit all cache keys and panel flags. ensure tests cover "fast switch" flows. add a unit test that simulates parallel preview responses with mismatched envelope headers.
oah: once staging flag looks good we'll roll strict namespacing to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over a week. also plan a one-off backfill to correct any telemetry mis-attribution.
cheng: also consider tightening default TTL for prefetched envelopes when panel has sensitive data (tables, events). shorter TTL reduces blast radius.
devops-bot: alert: leaked_row_count > 0 for org 12 reported at 2026-03-19T08:33:12Z. paging eng-platform on-call.
ella: i'm oncall, investigating now. i'll attach HARs, small repro script, and sample cache keys to the ticket.
sam: after hotfix, we should run a targeted synthetic fast-switch load test (simulate 200 switches/sec) to ensure no regression. i'll own the load test.
noah: tiny API debate: do we keep envelope headers mutable or make envelope opaque and store org metadata only in cache metadata? i vote opaque to reduce accidental exposure.
cheng: opaque is safer but requires more plumbing when we need to render metadata in UI. tradeoff table needed.
ella: for now prioritize safety: make envelope opaque and require explicit render binding that injects X-Console-Org at finalization time.
sam: noted. i'll add tasks and timeline to the ticket. update here when staging results available.
